replies.text:
Check of commonly missed items:

- Automated abuse (sign-in, email/SMS flooding, mass sign-up, scraping): design has no such entry point — only "Our internal agent can discover and install new MCP servers from a public registry at runtime". Not applicable.
- Staff/admin screens rendering other people's content: no screens or uploads described (`fileUpload: false`). Not applicable.
- Privileged actions with no record: design says installs happen "without a deploy" — already covered by listed threat 7 (no record of which tool version acted).
- Cacheable personal/financial documents: no documents or pages described, `dataClasses: []`. Not applicable.
- Attacker text into logs/CSV/emails/headers: nothing in the design states logging, export or email of tool data. Not applicable (poisoned metadata into the prompt is already listed threat 5).
- Single-reviewer items: the rug-pull / no-pinning family (items 2, 3, 6) attacks re-resolution of an already-used server from the same "public registry at runtime", which is a different moment and a different attack from the unvetted first install in listed threat 2 — not covered. Items 1 and 5 restate listed threats 5 and 2. Item 4 (poisoned output into memory) depends on persisted memory the design never mentions — excluded.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-08",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["internal AI agent", "MCP server install/discovery", "public MCP registry"],
    "dataStores": [],
    "externalServices": ["public MCP registry"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["internal agent host ↔ public registry"],
    "dataClasses": [],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": true
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Rug pull: a server that was fine before serves malicious code on the next runtime install",
      "scenario": "A publisher (or someone who takes over the registry account) ships a benign MCP server the agent already uses, then pushes a new build. Because the agent re-resolves and installs from the public registry at runtime with no pinned version or digest, the next install or restart silently swaps trusted tool code for a backdoor. No human action, deploy or review happens at that moment, so even a server someone once eyeballed turns hostile and acts with the agent's identity across every later task.",
      "component": "MCP server install from public registry",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "medium", "reach": "all", "harm": "takeover" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Our internal agent can discover and install new MCP servers from a public registry at runtime so it can use new tools without a deploy." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V10.3.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-494"],
      "plainLanguage": "A tool the agent already trusts can be quietly updated to a malicious version, because the agent re-downloads it from the public registry with no version or checksum locked in.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Pin and verify MCP server versions on every install",
        "given": "an MCP server the agent has used before",
        "when": "the agent installs or restarts it from the public registry at runtime",
        "then": "it must resolve only an explicitly pinned version and verify the package digest/signature against the recorded value, refusing to run and alerting when the artifact differs from the approved one"
      }
    }
  ]
}
